quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a road with good traction, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on a road with good traction, keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle should stay under control if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: Your body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank 8 drinks 4 hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals about 4 drinks remaining in the system.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Is not worth doing.
Does not mean they will yield to you.
Means the driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact with another driver means they will give you the right-of-way. They may not yield even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns solid yellow, you should:

options.text: Get ready to stop.
Speed up.
Put the vehicle in reverse and back up.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you can stop safely before entering the intersection, do so.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light when:

options.text: You see a police officer.
Another vehicle is following too closely.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your turn signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Another vehicle is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is tailgating you. They may not see the hazard ahead that is making you slow down. Also flash your brake light before slowing in unexpected places.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content is affected by three main factors: how much alcohol is consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. Sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have an effect.

questions.question: An integrated braking system:

options.text: Applies some rear braking when you use the front brake.
Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both brakes when either one is used.
Remembers the braking force you usually use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system is a type of linked braking system. When you use the rear brake, it automatically applies some front braking too. Check your motorcycle's manual for details about your specific braking system.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol on the body is:

options.text: Better riding ability.
Slower body functions.
More nervousness.
More alertness.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down and damages both physical and mental body functions.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake and then squeeze it again quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake immediately and completely. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Never.
Only during the day.
Only at night.
Both day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials helps other drivers see you at all times.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop completely, then go only if it is safe.
Go carefully through the intersection. You may not need to stop.
Stop only if there is traffic on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must always come to a complete stop. Then proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Kick the dog.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Turn around the dog.
Ride slowly toward the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slowly toward the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. Downshift and approach the dog slowly. As you get near, speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: Why is it good to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will see less of the road and stay more focused.
You will have more time to react if other drivers move unexpectedly.
You can follow the next vehicle more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react if other drivers move unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards. You will have more time to react and more room to turn if needed.

questions.question: What color are work area signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters or symbols.
White with red letters or symbols.
Blue with white letters or symbols.
Green with white letters or symbols.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange with black letters or symbols.
questions.explanation: Work area signs are orange with black letters and symbols. Slow down in work areas and follow all signs, signals, and instructions from workers.

questions.question: What should your riding clothes protect you from?

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Good clothing also protects you if you crash.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift to neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: The center of a lane has an oily strip from car drippings. Is it safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Never safe.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this strip still provides enough grip for motorcycles. The strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can often ride around it while staying in the center lane.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know they see you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee they will let you go when they should.
It guarantees they will let you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will let you go when they should.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers sometimes look directly at motorcyclists but do not see them.

questions.question: How should you brake on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Brake hard on the front to prevent the front wheel from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake gently to avoid locking the front wheel. Use light pressure on the rear brake.
